hypothesis: Registered after the adversarial review of the paper draft (2-3 Nov 2026), which asked for: compute-matched comparisons (E63), generation quality (E64), checkpoint selection without the exact score (E65), a stronger structured neural baseline (E66) and a vector-state proof of concept (E67). The user said 'Then go build those experiments'. Registered before any E63-E67 code was written or run. The draft counts parameter updates: EM iterations against SGD steps. One EM iteration is a full BP pass over the data plus an M-step (0.7-4.7 s on one CPU thread in E56), one SGD step is one minibatch (about 15 ms for BiGRU in E03), so update counts say nothing about compute. E63 measures seconds per update for every arm on the same hardware and puts the frozen validation curves on a wall-clock axis.
design: The Laplace chain of E03 (alpha = 0.85, L = 32, variance 1, Laplace innovations), E03's bundles (e03._cell_common, tags exp31-*), the twelve log-spaced levels t = 0.05 ... 3, the 401-point grid on [-8, 8]. PART timing (new runs, dev seed 10000, never a confirmatory seed): for N in (32, 128, 512, 2048), on ONE CPU thread (torch and BLAS), the median over 3 repetitions after one warm-up of: seconds per EM iteration (E-step over the N one-view noisy sequences of e03._one_view_groups plus the M-step) for em_bp (E30's mixture, C = 8), spline and energy (E56's recipes, energy width 16); seconds per clean M-step for clean_energy (E58's energy_h16 on the clean histogram, plus the one-off histogram time); seconds per SGD step at batch 64 for E03's six screened networks (median over 200 steps after 20 warm-up); and use-time seconds per test sequence over the twelve levels for BP on the 401 grid and for each network's forward pass. An optional part timing_gpu repeats the network steps and BP on one GPU. PART curves (no new fits, in the reader): the frozen validation curves (E56 val_curve for spline and energy, E02a val_curve for the C = 8 mixture, E58 val_curve for clean energy_h16, E03 val_curve for the networks) are put on a wall-clock axis, wall(c) = c x seconds per update at that N. Time to a target = the wall-clock of the FIRST checkpoint whose validation error is at or below the target (conservative: no interpolation between checkpoints).

predeclared_predictions.P1: Time to the networks' accuracy, noisy data: at N = 2048 the noisy-EM energy kernel (E56 curve) reaches the validation error of BiGRU's selected checkpoint in less wall-clock than BiGRU needs to reach it, in >= 12/16 seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P2: Time to the networks' accuracy, clean data: the clean-ML energy kernel (E58 curve) reaches BiGRU's selected validation error in less wall-clock than BiGRU at N = 128, 512 and 2048, in >= 12/16 seeds at each N.
predeclared_predictions.P3: Full training cost, the honest direction: at N = 2048 the noisy-EM energy kernel's wall-clock to ITS selected checkpoint exceeds BiGRU's wall-clock to its selected checkpoint, in >= 12/16 seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P4: Use time: BP on the 401 grid costs more per test sequence (twelve levels) than BiGRU's forward pass, by more than a factor 10, on one CPU thread at batch 2048.

descriptive.D1: Seconds per update for every arm and N, and the ratio EM iteration / SGD step.
descriptive.D2: Validation error against wall-clock for every arm, one figure per N.
descriptive.D3: Analytic operation counts: an EM iteration ~ N (L-1) N_g^2 multiply-adds for the E-step plus the M-step's grid evaluations; an SGD step ~ 6 x parameters x batch x L.

predeclared_analysis: tools/core/read_e63.py. Gates: timing rows for every (arm, N); every frozen curve used is the one of the frozen row with the same (seed, N, arm) as the paper's tables. A seed whose curve never reaches the target counts AGAINST P1/P2. Paired by seed; no bootstrap.
seeds: timing: dev seed 10000; curves: the frozen confirmatory seeds 0-15 of E02a, E03, E56 and E58
budget_rule: timing only; no fit is extended or rerun.
provenance_note: The curves are frozen outputs (E02a, E03, E56, E58); E63 adds only timings.
resources: About 2 CPU-h (one exclusive node, one thread); timing_gpu about 0.5 GPU-h.
